title: Test small, decide 'yes' first
principle: Test small first, and decide beforehand what result means yes.

screens.text: In October 2007, two former Amazon staff started Flipkart in Bengaluru, selling only books. In its first year, it made 20 shipments.

screens.prompt: Why would Flipkart start with books alone, not everything?

options.label: To learn cheaply before betting big

screens.why: One small range let them learn orders, delivery and buyers. They handed out bookmarks outside a Bengaluru bookshop. Phones and electronics came only in 2010.

screens.title: Write 'yes' down first
screens.text: Test small. Before you start, write the number that means 'yes', and the date you'll check. Then let the number decide, not hope.

screens.prompt: Which 'yes' line tells you a new lunch service can really work?

options.label: 120 paid lunches in 4 weeks, ₹40 left on each

screens.why: Enquiries are weaker than payments, and payments with no margin can still lose money. A number, a date and money: you can't argue with it later.

wrong.a: Asking costs people nothing. Count what they pay for.
wrong.b: Better, but 120 lunches that each lose ₹5 is still a loss. Add what each one leaves.

screens.title: Sana's cake stall
screens.text: Sana wants a cake stall at an office park. It costs ₹15,000 a month, and each cake box leaves her ₹60.

screens.prompt: The park is open 25 days a month. How many boxes a day just covers the stall?
screens.why: ₹15,000 ÷ ₹60 = 250 boxes a month. 250 ÷ 25 days = 10 a day. So her 'yes' must be above 10, or she works for free.

wrong.a: That's a month. Split it over 25 days.
wrong.c: Work it out: ₹15,000 ÷ ₹60 = 250 a month, then ÷ 25 days.

screens.prompt: Sana tests for four weeks and sells 7 a day. Her friend says, 'Close to 10. Go!' What do you say?

options.label: Change the offer and test again

screens.why: At 7 a day she's 3 boxes short. 3 × ₹60 × 25 days = ₹4,500 lost every month. Try a new price or spot, then test again.

wrong.c: Moving the line after the test is how hope wins. The sum didn't change.

screens.prompt: A second salon costs ₹12 lakh. Neeta tests first: one rented chair in a gym, ₹8,000 a month for 3 months. What share is that?
screens.why: 3 × ₹8,000 = ₹24,000. ₹24,000 ÷ ₹12,00,000 = 2%. She risks 2 rupees to learn before she risks 100.

wrong.b: ₹24,000 is much smaller than that. 20% would be ₹2,40,000.
wrong.c: 0.2% would be just ₹2,400. The test is ₹24,000.

items.text: Cook 20 plates for one office lunch

screens.why: A test is cheap and quick to undo, while a bet locks your money in. Do the tests first, and let them earn you the bet.

screens.prompt: Put a good test in order.
steps: Write the yes number and the date
screens.why: The yes number comes before the test. Every Sunday, count the two or three numbers that decide. Let them decide, not hope.

screens.setup: Pooja wants a 6 am women-only batch at her gym. A full new floor would cost ₹5 lakh. Some members say they'd 'surely join'.
screens.question: What do you do?

options.label: Build the floor. Members asked for it
options.outcome: The floor opens, but only eight women come in the first month. ₹5 lakh is now in walls and mats.
options.why: Saying 'I'd join' is free. She bet big on words, not payments.
options.better: Run one paid batch first, with a yes number.

options.label: One 6 am batch for 6 weeks. Yes = 20 paid
options.outcome: By week 6, 23 women have paid. Now the floor is a bet with proof behind it.
options.why: She tested cheaply in the space she had, and wrote the yes number first.

options.label: Do a members' survey first
options.outcome: 70% tick 'yes'. She still doesn't know who will pay at 6 am.
options.why: A survey costs little, but it measures words.
options.better: Ask for payment. That is the real test.

screens.text: Write the ___ that means yes ___ the test starts.
screens.why: Decide the line first. After the test, it's too easy to move it.

summary: Start with a small, cheap version of the idea.
Write the yes number and the date before you start.
Don't move the line after the test. Change the offer and test again.

cards.front: Your test hit 8 against a yes number of 12. What now?
cards.back: The line was set for a reason. Change the offer, not the line.

cards.front: Stall rent ₹9,000 a month. Each sale leaves ₹30. Open 30 days. Sales a day to break even?

sources.label: How two IITians built Flipkart, from bookmarks outside bookstores (Business Today, 9 May 2018)
